outcome: Incidence of small for gestational age
Mode of delivery (spontaneous, assisted, or caesarean section)
cohort: The study participants were Gestational Diabetes mellitus (GDM) patients, aged 26-35 years, receiving either metformin or insulin therapy.
finding: The study found no statistically significant differences in maternal complications, neonatal complications, or mode of delivery between GDM patients treated with metformin and those treated with insulin, suggesting metformin is equally effective.
mod_finding: There were no statistically significant differences in the mode of delivery between the metformin and insulin treatment groups.
